classification.difficultyReason: Reflect the right half of a tangent graph while preserving its asymptotes, negative branches and restricted endpoints.

answer.short: An even graph with zeros at $x=-\pi,0,\pi$ and vertical asymptotes $x=\pm\frac{\pi}{2}$. The central branches are positive; the outer branches are negative.
answer.worked: Sketch $y=\tan x$ for $0\le x\le\pi$, excluding $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$. Keep this right half and reflect a copy across the $y$-axis. Mark closed endpoints at $(-\pi,0)$ and $(\pi,0)$, and vertical asymptotes $x=\pm\frac{\pi}{2}$. The graph has a sharp point at $(0,0)$.

spec.description: Symmetric tangent branches with two dashed vertical asymptotes, closed outer endpoints and a sharp point at the origin.
spec.mathematics: y=tan(abs(x)), -pi<=x<=pi, x!=+-pi/2; positive for 0<abs(x)<pi/2 and negative for pi/2<abs(x)<pi.
